finding: Page 1:2 is a component LIBRARY, not a set of product screens — it holds 118 component nodes and zero user-facing flows, so it must be audited on variant/state/token coverage, never on 'does the user need this screen'.
evidence: Full-depth walk of 1:2: 25 COMPONENT_SET + 93 COMPONENT = 118 component nodes, plus 11 documentation FRAMEs (8:48 'Accent guard — proof', 20:6 'GATE A — does 320 hold?', 91:6 'Icons — 30 Lucide, real geometry', 469:3961 'Disabled ships its tooltip — rule', 685:116 'Presence — the four shapes', 699:440 'Topbar — every state', 1034:750 'Focus — the ring rule', 11:36, 14:45, 16:27, 17:41). No frame on the page is a product screen. Six TEXT headers (1054:13380-1054:13391) index it as Editor Component Sets / Editor Components / Dashboard Component Sets / Dashboard Components / Icons / Documentation & Showcase.
recommend: Audit and maintain 1:2 as a library page — variant coverage, state coverage, naming, token binding — and keep product screens on the per-surface pages (1:3 Editor, 397:2 / 988:2 Dashboard).

finding: The focus ring is defined four incompatible ways across this page and the code, and no two agree — the single most-repeated interaction state in the library has no canonical value.
evidence: (1) Rule text 1034:751 verbatim: 'Focus ring: 2px white offset + 2px accent, never removed. focus/ring-width = 2.' (2) Every focus variant actually drawn on the page — 17 of them — uses DROP_SHADOW #1A56DB alpha 0.25, spread 3, radius 0, offset 0,0: a 3px solid-ish halo hugging the control with no offset gap (9:10, 9:22, 9:34, 9:46, 9:58, 9:70, 9:82, 9:94, 10:8, 12:24, 697:434, 1034:738, 1034:740, 1034:742, 1034:744, 1034:746, 1034:748). (3) packages/editor/src/themes/tokens.generated.css:203 --bk-shadow-focus: 0 0 0 2px rgba(26, 86, 219, 0.30) — 2px at 30%, not 3px at 25%. (4) packages/editor/src/themes/design-system/a11y.css:99-105 comments 'Figma "Buildrick — Product" focus spec: 2px accent border/outline, NO halo' then applies outline: 2px solid var(--bk-accent); outline-offset: 2px — while buttonTheme.ts:36,40 puts the halo back on buttons via tw:focus:[box-shadow:var(--bk-shadow-focus)].
recommend: Pick one focus contract (the a11y.css 2px accent outline at 2px offset is the only one that matches the page's own written rule), redraw all 17 focus variants to it, and reconcile --bk-shadow-focus and buttonTheme.ts to the same value in the same commit.

finding: Dashboard / Button draws its disabled state as the brand colour at 50% opacity — the exact anti-pattern the editor's own button theme documents as a fixed defect, leaving a dead control still dressed as the primary action.
evidence: 981:668 (Primary md Disabled) fill=#1A56DB opacity=0.5; 981:674 (Primary sm) same; 981:692 / 981:698 (Danger) fill=#C81E1E opacity=0.5. Label text stays #FFFFFF at full opacity. packages/editor/src/editor/chrome-ui/buttonTheme.ts:20-31 records the fix verbatim: 'opacity-50, which left every disabled primary as the brand blue at half strength — a dead control still dressed as the primary action (boards 781:4526 / 784:4287 draw a grey chip)' and now emits tw:disabled:bg-[var(--bk-bg-subtle)] tw:disabled:text-[var(--bk-ink-muted)]. The editor's own Button set already complies: 9:12 / 9:24 / 9:84 / 9:96 fill=#E5E7EB.
recommend: Redraw the four Dashboard / Button disabled variants as the grey chip the editor set and buttonTheme.ts already use (bg --bk-bg-subtle, ink --bk-ink-muted), not brand colour at half opacity.

finding: Every primary button on the page sits one step lighter than the code's accent ramp: the boards rest on #1C64F2 and hover to #1A56DB, while the tokens rest on #1A56DB and hover to #1E429F.
evidence: Measured fills — 9:6/9:18 (primary rest) #1C64F2, 9:8/9:20 (primary hover) #1A56DB; 981:664/981:670 (Dashboard Primary Default) #1C64F2, 981:666/981:672 (Hover) #1A56DB. tokens.generated.css:81-82 --bk-accent: #1A56DB; --bk-accent-hover: #1E429F. The boards' hover value is the token's REST value, so the whole ramp is shifted one Flowbite step. Root CLAUDE.md pins the single accent at #1A56DB with hover #1E429F.
recommend: Rebind both Button sets' primary rest to #1A56DB (--bk-accent) and hover to #1E429F (--bk-accent-hover) so the drawn ramp is the token ramp.

finding: Neither Button set draws the code's five-role variant vocabulary: the editor set renames one role and omits another, and the Dashboard set omits two.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/chrome-ui/Button.tsx:24 export type ButtonVariant = "primary" | "secondary" | "ghost" | "link" | "danger", documented at :7 as 'the five-role vocabulary two independent audits found'. Figma 9:102 variantGroupProperties Kind = [primary, secondary, ghost, destructive] — 'destructive' where the code says 'danger', and no 'link'. Figma 981:700 Kind = [Primary, Ghost, Danger] — no 'secondary', no 'link'. buttonTheme.ts:33 defines a real `link` recipe, so the role ships.
recommend: Rename the editor set's `destructive` to `danger` to match the prop value, and add the missing `link` variant to both sets (and `secondary` to the Dashboard set) — per the brief's precedence rule the code contract owns these names.

finding: The icon library is 67 components under two competing naming conventions with 11 glyphs drawn more than once, three of them exact same-size duplicates.
evidence: Full walk: 67 COMPONENT nodes matching icon/ — 38 use the spaced form 'Icon / name', 29 use the tight form 'icon/name'. 11 glyphs appear twice or more; three are duplicates at identical 24px: chevron-left (91:30 vs 681:4334), ellipsis (91:49 vs 681:4343), bell (91:67 vs 681:4338, plus 980:673 at 18px). The rest differ only by size suffix (search 91:36 24px vs 980:669 16px; plus, trash-2, settings, image, lock, triangle-alert, chevron-right). Note 91:8 justifies per-size drawing ('24 box, 2 stroke, round caps — do not rescale the stroke'), which covers the size variants but not the three identical ones.
recommend: Settle on one naming convention (the tight 'icon/name-<size>' form carries the size, so prefer it), and merge the three identical 24px pairs so a glyph has one master.

finding: Two different focus-ring geometries and three different blues are in use across the page's focusable components, and one component carries both geometries at once.
evidence: Geometry A — DROP_SHADOW #1A56DB spread 3, no offset: Button x8, Input 10:8, Checkbox 12:24, Dashboard/Button x6, Icon button 697:434 (17 variants). Geometry B — a true 2px OUTSIDE stroke, no shadow: Toggle 14:10, Radio 14:18, Select 14:29, all stroked #1C64F2 w2 align=OUTSIDE. Icon button 697:434 has BOTH (DROP_SHADOW #1A56DB sp3 AND stroke #1A56DB w2 OUTSIDE). Three accent blues appear in focus treatment alone: #1A56DB (halo), #1C64F2 (Toggle/Radio/Select stroke), #3F83F8 (Input focus stroke 10:8).
recommend: Converge on one geometry and one blue (--bk-accent #1A56DB) for focus across all 20 focus variants; drop the duplicate treatment on Icon button 697:434.

screen: Tree row / Card · media / Nav item

screen: Card / site vs Dashboard / Site card
finding: SiteCard is forked in Figma and in code at the same time — two nodes and two implementations for one object, and the editor's copy of both is the dead one.
evidence: Figma: 17:9 'Card / site' (inside 17:41 Molecules — content) and 997:705 'Dashboard / Site card'. Code: packages/editor/src/editor/chrome-ui/SiteCard.tsx (0 production consumers) and packages/dashboard/components/dashboard/site-card.tsx:32 export function SiteCard, consumed at packages/dashboard/components/dashboard/recent-sites.tsx:6,26. The site card is a dashboard object — sites are listed in the dashboard, not inside the editor chrome.

finding: The page's own index undercounts itself — ten real components are buried one level inside showcase frames and are invisible to the section headers that are supposed to enumerate the library.
evidence: Header 1054:13380/13381 reads 'Editor Component Sets · 14 items'; the true count of non-Dashboard COMPONENT_SETs is 19 — the five uncounted are Toggle 14:14, Radio 14:20, Select 14:37 (inside 14:45 'Atoms — controls'), Nav item 16:26 (inside 16:27), Comment row 17:40 (inside 17:41). Header 1054:13382/13383 reads 'Editor Components · 7 items'; the true count is 14 — the seven uncounted are Tooltip 14:43, Panel header 16:6, Section header 16:16, Card / media 17:6, Card / site 17:9, Empty state 17:18, Progress row 17:23. Dashboard counts (6 sets / 12 components) and Documentation (11) are accurate.
recommend: Either promote the nested components to the flat section bands so the index is true, or restate the two editor labels as 19 and 14 — right now a reader taking the index at face value misses ten components.

finding: Two icon components sit at the page origin inside the Editor Component Sets header band, hundreds of pixels from the icon section, and fall outside every section count.
evidence: 1695:755 'Icon / crosshair' at x=1104,y=0 and 1695:760 'Icon / corner-left-up' at x=1140,y=0, both 24x24. The Editor Component Sets header 1054:13380 sits at 0,0 and its sets start at y=60; the icon band runs at y=13204-13296. Neither is inside 91:6 'Icons — 30 Lucide' (which holds exactly 30) nor counted by 'Icons · 29 items' (1054:13388/13389).
recommend: Move both into the 91:6 icon grid and update its title and the section count from 30/29 to the new totals.

finding: The editor and Dashboard halves of one library use opposite casing for identical variant values, so the same state is spelled two ways in one file.
evidence: Editor sets use lowercase: Button Kind=[primary, secondary, ghost, destructive] State=[rest, hover, focus, disabled, loading]; Input State=[rest, focus, filled, error, disabled]; Icon button State=[rest, hover, focus, disabled]. Dashboard sets use Titlecase: Dashboard / Button Kind=[Primary, Ghost, Danger] State=[Default, Hover, Disabled, Focus]; Dashboard / Nav item State=[Default, Active, Hover]; Dashboard / Pill Tone=[Neutral, Success, Warning, Error, Accent]; Dashboard / Section tab State=[Default, Active]. The rest/Default split is the same state under two names.
recommend: Normalise all variant property keys and values to the editor's lowercase form, which matches the code's prop values (ButtonVariant is lowercase).

finding: The size names collide across the two halves — 'md' resolves to two different heights and the Dashboard's 'sm' is the same pixel height as the editor's 'md'.
evidence: Measured heights: editor Button 9:102 sm=28px, md=32px. Dashboard / Button 981:700 sm=32px, md=40px. So Dashboard sm (32) == editor md (32), and 'md' means 32 or 40 depending on which half of the same library you are reading. 40px is flowbite's stock h-10 default, which packages/editor/CLAUDE.md already flags as the leak that put 40px controls in 28px rows.
recommend: Either give the two halves distinct size scales with distinct names, or state the pixel value in the variant label, so no one reads 'md' off the wrong half.

finding: The auth surface ships seventeen components and the library draws one — every auth primitive a designer would need to change is undesigned.
evidence: packages/dashboard/components/auth/ contains auth-art, auth-back-link, auth-button, auth-card, auth-divider, auth-icon, auth-input, auth-logo, auth-message, auth-social-buttons, form-banner, inline-error, otp-input, password-strength, resend-timer, social-button, turnstile-widget (17 files). Page 1:2's only auth node is the composed set 1017:810 'Dashboard / Auth error' (9 Reason variants, all 9 of which do exist in dashboard code). No OTP input, password-strength meter, resend timer, social button or Turnstile widget component exists anywhere on 1:2 — and the abandoned page 500:3 draws OTP boxes and a password field, so the need was recognised and then lost.
recommend: Add otp-input, password-strength, resend-timer, social-button and turnstile-widget to the Dashboard half of the library, built from the shipped code.

finding: State coverage is lopsided across the two halves: the Dashboard gets five shared state components, the editor gets one, so every editor panel invents its own error and loading treatment.
evidence: Dashboard half: 985:682 State — empty, 985:694 State — error, 985:707 State — denied, 985:719 State — loading (list), 985:729 State — loading (table); mirrored in code by packages/dashboard/components/states/{state-empty,state-error,state-denied,state-loading,state-action}.tsx. Editor half: 17:18 'Empty state' only. packages/editor/src/editor/chrome-ui/ has EmptyState.tsx and Skeleton.tsx but no error or denied state component (grep for 'denied|ErrorState' across chrome-ui returns nothing).
recommend: Draw editor-side error / denied / loading state components as siblings of 17:18, or state explicitly that the editor reuses the Dashboard five, which nothing currently records.

finding: Badge and Dashboard / Pill are the same object under two names with two property keys and four mismatched fills, and only one of them has a border.
evidence: 12:16 'Badge' Kind=[neutral, success, warning, danger, pro], every variant carrying a 1px stroke: neutral #E5E7EB/#9CA3AF, success #DEF7EC/#0E9F6E, warning #FDF6B2/#C27803, danger #FDE8E8/#E02424, pro #EDEBFE/#1C64F2. 982:694 'Dashboard / Pill' Tone=[Neutral, Success, Warning, Error, Accent], no strokes at all: #F3F4F6, #DEF7EC, #FDFDEA, #FDE8E8, #E1EFFE. Neutral and warning fills differ (#E5E7EB vs #F3F4F6; #FDF6B2 vs #FDFDEA); only success and danger/Error agree. The pro tint #EDEBFE is the allowlisted PRO purple, not a Gate 18 violation.
recommend: Pick one name (Badge), one property key (Kind), one fill per tone, and one border decision; keep pro/Accent as the deliberate extra role in each half.

finding: One variant inside the Badge set is 2px taller than its four siblings, so a row of badges does not sit on a common baseline.
evidence: Measured heights in 12:16: neutral 12:6 = 20px, success 12:8 = 20px, warning 12:10 = 22px, danger 12:12 = 20px, pro 12:14 = 20px.
recommend: Set 12:10 to 20px to match the set.

finding: Page 500:2 is not a Buildrik library — it is a foreign UI-kit reference sheet with no component nodes at all, and nothing in the file can consume it.
evidence: 500:2 holds one child, 500:3 'Element' (1440x1024, 52 children). Full walk: COMPONENT=0, COMPONENT_SET=0, INSTANCE=0, FRAME=152 — nothing is a master, so nothing can instance it. Rendered content is generic kit material: a date picker reading 'August 2024', a phone country picker, a tag input, OTP boxes, a rich-text toolbar, a Day/Week/Month/Year segmented control, a drag-and-drop upload. Child names use a vocabulary Buildrik does not have: 'Button / Tonal', 'Button / Gray', 'Input Small / Warning', 'Phone / Country'.
recommend: Rename to 'ARCHIVE — foreign UI kit reference (not Buildrik)' so nobody mistakes it for the library; never delete.

finding: Page 510:2 is a wholesale paste of a purchased admin template, unrelated to Buildrik and inert as a library.
evidence: 510:2 holds six SECTIONs (512:33 Components 22836px wide, 512:9109 Layouts, 512:12532 Maps, 512:13097 Form, 512:16530 Tables, 512:18942 Extended UI). Full walk: COMPONENT=0, COMPONENT_SET=0, INSTANCE=0, FRAME=4902. Frame names are third-party plugin surfaces Buildrik does not ship: Elements/Extended/Sweet Alert, Elements/Extended/Swiper, Elements/Extended/Tippy Tooltip, Elements/Extended/Lightbox, Elements/Extended/Nestable, Elements/Extended/Player, Elements/Extended/Tour Page, Elements/Maps/Google Maps, Elements/Maps/Vector Maps.

finding: Page 1:2 contains no design for the editor's Components PANEL — the surface a user opens to manage saved components. It is purely a primitives library, so pointing the Components module at this page would leave the panel undesigned.
evidence: All 118 component nodes on 1:2 enumerated: not one is a saved-component card, library grid, create-component flow, detach confirm, or a panel empty/loading/error state. A text search of every TEXT node on 1:2 for /component|instance|detach|master|reusable|saved/i returns 35 hits and every one is either design-system vocabulary (1054:13380 'Editor Component Sets', 699:443 '1 component · 60 instances · consumes Button, Icon button, Save status, Presence, Avatar', 469:3963 'The tooltip is its own component'), Save-status sample copy ('Saved 2m ago', 697:443), or the single Brand-drawer row 20:85. Nothing addresses managing saved components.
recommend: Do NOT redirect the Components module to page 1:2. Promote the editor page's existing Components boards (641:2546, 641:2599, 642:3112, 778:4173, 781:4433, 1138:13394, 1170:4777, 1170:4792) out of the review scratch section into a module of their own.

finding: The library draws the entry point to components as a row inside the Brand drawer, and the code records the same intent, but the destination it points at lives in a review scratch section on another page — the door is designed, the room is filed as scratch.
evidence: 20:84 is a row in 20:56 '320 — Brand' reading 'Components' (20:85) with count '27' (20:87) and a chevron (20:88), sitting between 'Classes 12' and 'Typography'. packages/editor/src/editor/rail/tabsConfig.ts records the same routing verbatim: 'components → shortcut ⇧A + ⌘K ("Open Components panel"); folds into Brand · components per the design in a later phase', and RAIL_FIGMA lists six rail items (add, layers, pages, assets, content, design) with components deliberately off-rail. The Rail icons set 11:36 correctly draws exactly those six (Icon / insert, layers, pages, media, content, brand) — checked, no gap there.
recommend: When the Components boards are promoted out of scratch, wire 20:84 to the module's entry board so the Brand-drawer row has a destination in the prototype, not just in a code comment.

finding: The editor Button carries two stacked black drop shadows that its Dashboard twin does not, so the same role reads as raised in one half of the library and flat in the other.
evidence: 9:6 (primary sm rest) and 9:8 (hover) both carry DROP_SHADOW #000000 sp0 r2 off0,1 plus DROP_SHADOW #000000 sp-1 r3 off0,1 — Tailwind's stock shadow pair. 981:664 / 981:666 (Dashboard Primary Default / Hover) have effects=none. packages/editor/CLAUDE.md Gates 11/12 require chrome shadows to come from var(--bk-shadow-*) or be none; the only raised token is --bk-shadow-raised: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.08) (tokens.generated.css:200), which is one shadow, not two, and lighter.
recommend: Replace the stacked pair with --bk-shadow-raised or remove it, and make both halves agree.

finding: The focus rule frame cites a token as its authority that nothing in the codebase reads — the rule rests on a dead token.
evidence: 1034:751 reads '... focus/ring-width = 2.' The corresponding tokens exist at tokens.generated.css:156-157 (--bk-focus-ring-width: 2px; --bk-focus-ring-offset: 2px) but a repo-wide grep across *.css, *.ts and *.tsx excluding tokens.generated returns zero consumers for either. The focus treatment that actually ships comes from --bk-shadow-focus (:203) and the a11y.css outline rule, neither of which reads the ring-width token.
recommend: Either wire --bk-focus-ring-width / --bk-focus-ring-offset into a11y.css so the rule's citation is true, or cite --bk-shadow-focus instead.

finding: Thirteen components that ship in the editor's single import surface have no node anywhere on the library page, so the most-used overlay and chrome primitives cannot be designed against.
evidence: Exported from packages/editor/src/editor/chrome-ui/index.ts and present as real files, but absent from the full-depth walk of 1:2: Toast, Popover/Menu/MenuItem/MenuGroup, CommandPalette, Tabs (only Dashboard / Section tab 989:7133 exists), Toolbar, Chip, IssueChip, Kbd, Spinner, Skeleton (SkeletonListItem/StudioSkeleton/SkeletonBlock), BreakpointSwitcher, Footer, Textarea. Drawer exists as 19:46 but only as three Layout variants (list/grid/table) with no open/closed or loading state. Scope note: this absence is verified for page 1:2 only — I did not exhaustively walk pages 0:1, 1:3, 397:2 or 988:2 at full depth.
recommend: Prioritise Toast, Popover/Menu and CommandPalette — they are the overlay surfaces users hit constantly and the ones most likely to drift without a master.
